extracted.intended_audience: students, journalists, editors, and media scholars interested in newsworthiness and editorial decision-making
extracted.subtask_description: A catalogue of criteria used to judge the newsworthiness of events and stories across multiple academic and professional frameworks; useful for editors, reporters, and media-studies analysis. Covers classical Galtung & Ruge factors, later process-related and digital-era additions, and discursive critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: How often an event occurs relative to the news cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally one of Galtung & Ruge's 12 factors: events that fit the routine frequency of news production are more likely to be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an event reaches a size, scale or intensity that makes it newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: events must pass a certain threshold of magnitude or significance to be selected as news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of facts or interpretation—events that are easily framed/understood are preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: unambiguous events are easier for news organizations to process and present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the event connects to the audience's existing knowledge, values or interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: culturally familiar or meaningful events are more likely to be selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compatibility of an event with reporters' or editors' expectations, routines or stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: events that 'fit' prevailing narratives and frames are more likely to be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty or surprise value of an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: surprising or deviant events attract coverage because they break expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a story is ongoing or can be linked to an existing storyline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by Galtung & Ruge and reiterated in process-related values: ongoing stories gain momentum via media infrastructure and are more likely to receive follow-up coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition
rubrics_metrics.description: How a story fits into the editor's overall package or the available space/time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge and process-related notes: editors balance content across pages/slots; composition affects selection to create a coherent mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Elite Nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the event involves or references powerful / elite nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: events connected to elite countries are privileged in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Elite People
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the event involves prominent or influential people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: involvement of elites (politicians, leaders) increases newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a story can be told through individual protagonists or personal angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: stories that can be personalized (human faces, anecdotes) are more attractive for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of bad news, conflict, or negativity in an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galtung & Ruge: negative or conflictual events are more likely to be reported; appears also in common underlying categories as 'Negativity / Bad news'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial rivalry and competition between outlets shaping story selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A process-related value: outlets under competitive pressure may pursue stories that attract audiences or scoop rivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-option
rubrics_metrics.description: Marginal stories gaining coverage because they can be tied to a major narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-related: less prominent events are sometimes covered if they can be linked to an ongoing major story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-written or pre-packaged marginal stories prepared in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-related: newsrooms may select prefabricated items that fit slots or deadlines, affecting what appears as 'news'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency for pre-scheduled or predictable events to be covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-related: planned events (press conferences, elections) are more likely to receive coverage because timing and sourcing are reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured or perceived impact of a story—shareability, reader engagement, and effect on audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under process-related values: increasing emphasis on metrics such as shares, clicks, and engagement shapes selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline pressures and time available to produce a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-related: tight schedules influence which stories can be produced and how thoroughly they are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical staff and technical resources determining coverage feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-related: availability of reporters, cameras, translation, or travel resources affects whether a story is covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/Facticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for stories backed by raw data, figures, or verifiable facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-related: factual, data-driven stories are favored for perceived credibility and defensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Status or fame of the people, institutions or nations involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harcup & O'Neill (2001) addition and common category: prominent actors (celebrities, senior officials) increase newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good News
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive or uplifting stories that have news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harcup & O'Neill (2001) addition: not all news is negative; positive developments can be selected for their appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization-specific priorities and editorial agendas guiding selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harcup & O'Neill (2001): an outlet's own agenda shapes what it treats as news, beyond universal factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareability
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential for a story to be shared via social media (clicks, social spread).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harcup & O'Neill (2017): digital-era value emphasizing social distribution metrics as selection drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time or live nature of coverage; timeliness in the moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harcup & O'Neill (2017): digital newsrooms value immediacy—live updates and breaking coverage—when judging newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio-visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of arresting visuals, video or audio that enhance a story's appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harcup & O'Neill (2017) addition: audiovisual material (photos, video) increases a story's pick-up and prominence, especially online and TV.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values as constructed through discourse (Bednarek & Caple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that news values are not simply objective traits but are produced through language and editorial discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bednarek & Caple propose a discursive approach: newsworthiness is constructed by how stories are talked about and framed; primary analytic categories include relevance, impact, and meaningfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a story is pertinent or applicable to an audience or context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bednarek & Caple list relevance among primary discursive categories; overlaps with 'meaningfulness' and 'impact' but emphasizes contextual pertinence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect a story has on people's lives or on public affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed both as a common underlying category and as a Bednarek & Caple primary category; often operationalized as the potential for change, harm, influence, or material consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recency of the event; how current the information is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common underlying category: freshness and recency make stories more likely to be selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic or psychological closeness of the event to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common category: events nearer to the audience—geographically or culturally—are more salient.

rubrics_metrics.name: The unusual / Bizarreness / Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of oddness, novelty or bizarre quality that draws attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common underlying category: bizarre or unusual events attract interest because they deviate from norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of disagreement, contest, or struggle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common underlying category: conflict drives drama and narrative tension, increasing newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an issue is currently prominent in public discussion or agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common category: topicality—stories connected to current debates or trending issues—boost selection chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that appeal emotionally or via individual human experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common category: human-interest angles (emotion, personalization) attract readers and provide hookable narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualness
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of a story for visual presentation (images, video, graphics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common category and related to audio-visuals: visually striking stories are prioritized by TV and digital outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-driven metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of audience behavior and metrics (clicks, shares, engagement) in shaping editorial choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique/Caveat: the digital age has amplified audience metrics as a driver of news values, reshaping what editors treat as newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and organizational variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that news values vary across cultures and media organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques and caveats note that lists of criteria are not universal; selection practices differ by cultural context and by organizational priorities.
